messages:
maria: FYI — large bank (pilot) is asking for an anonymized audit-log stream for SOC2 evidence sharing with their internal auditors. they want: (1) PII redaction, (2) 13-month retention in eu region, (3) schema-compatible export to their SIEM. can we scope a pilot?
ajay: need clarity: by anonymized do they mean redaction (remove fields) or tokenization (hash/pseudonymize) so it can be re-linked by them later?
maria: they explicitly asked for non-reversible pseudonymization (hash + salt) so they can keep event id linkage but not raw emails/names. legal flagged re-linking risks.
samir: hashing + salt is OK if salt is customer-managed (BYOK-like) or we store salt in HSM. otherwise hashes could be reversible via rainbow tables. also need to decide if device IDs are considered PII.
lina: legal: for SOC2 auditors we need to provide provenance of processing (who did the pseudonymization and where). if we do this in EU region we must document key custody, KMS logs, and retention policy.
maria: pilot asks: 1) export endpoint that returns newline-delimited JSON events with PII fields replaced by hashed values, 2) retention TTL per-customer (13mo for this bank), 3) region-tagging and legal attestation doc.
ajay: doable but infra caveats: (a) export must preserve schema for their parsers — can't change field names. (b) we need a per-customer salt rotation plan. (c) will impact storage indexing/search costs if hashed fields still indexed.
samir: proposals: A) customer-provided salt (preferred) -> we never see it; B) Redwood-managed salt in HSM with audit logs -> we provide attestation. tradeoffs: A blocks us from doing any internal re-identification for support.
legal-team: preference for customer-managed salt for risk transfer, but operationally customers may object. include both in pilot and list differences in SOW.
ajay: ops question — can we add a retention override per export stream? need a flag in the export config: {"retention_days": 395, "region": "eu-west-1", "pseudonymization": "hash-salt", "salt_mode": "customer|redwood"}
ops-bot: deploy job queued: export-pilot-config v0.1 -> staging (ETA 4h). logs will appear in #eng-runtime.
maria: acceptance criteria for pilot: - exported stream contains same keys as prod events, with PII fields hashed; - customer can ingest into Splunk/Quartz with no schema changes; - we produce a legal attestation doc + KMS audit trail; - retention honors per-stream TTL and hard-deletes are verifiable.
lina: add legal hold override process for e-discovery; we need playbook for freezes that supersede TTL.
samir: security checklist for pilot: 1) threat model for hash leakage, 2) HSM audit logs enabled, 3) salt rotation doc, 4) SIEM integration test (verify no raw PII appears).
ajay: dev tasks: - add salt_mode flag to export API (owner: ajay) - wire per-stream retention in archival pipeline (owner: ops) - add attestation generator (owner: maria/legal) - create canary test with synthetic PII (owner: eng-test)
maria: timeline proposal: start pilot with bank in 3 sprints (6 weeks). checkpoints: week2 infra + legal attestation draft, week4 test ingestion, week6 go/no-go.
legal-team: i'll draft SOW + e-discovery addendum. confirm whether the attestation can say "Redwood performed pseudonymization using customer-managed key" vs "Redwood-managed" depending on salt_mode.
ajay: technical call with the customer's infra next Tue 10am. i'll book.
maria: thanks — thinking we should include a short FAQ for customers about irreversible pseudonymization vs reversible tokenization. keeps expectations clear. :thumbsup:
ajay: agree. adding a note that reversible tokenization requires escrow & stricter controls.
samir: one more: update the compliance roadmap doc to include this pilot as an "evidence export variant" entry so PMs see capacity and SLA implications.
maria: putting tasks into the pilot epic now. tagging folks. ping me if you need sample event payloads.
